## How to get an API key
Copper uses API key. The steps below follow Copper's own docs.
1.  Create a Copper account. API access starts on the Professional plan.
2.  Copper web app > System settings > API Keys > GENERATE API KEY; OAuth 2.0 for partner integrations
3.  Send it with every request: headers: X-PW-AccessToken: <API key>, X-PW-Application: developer\_api, X-PW-UserEmail: <email of key owner>, Content-Type: application/json.
4.  Make a first call: Atomically update the lead matching given criteria or create it. Match on name, email or a custom field (match.field\_name 'custom' with custom\_field\_definition\_id + value; the field must be available on Leads and filterable). 0 matches = create, 1 = update, >1 = 422 with matching IDs, >30 = 422 without IDs. Keep the key in an environment variable, never in the command.
```
curl -X PUT "https://api.copper.com/developer_api/v1/leads/upsert" \
-H "X-PW-AccessToken: $COPPER_API_KEY" \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
-d '{}'
```

title: Overview - Copper Developer API
snippet:
There are two ways to access the Copper Developer API: API keys and OAuth2.0. API Keys are suitable for individual users, while OAuth2.0 is the preferred approach for partner integrations.
## API Keys¶
The Dev API uses token based authentication. You have to include the token in the header of every request, along with the email address of the user who generated the token. Users can hold multiple valid tokens at the same time. Admins can see all user generated tokens and generate new ones.
To generate an API token, in the Copper web app go to System settings > API Keys and click the 'GENERATE API KEY' button. Copper allows you to label each key for its unique purpose. You'll need to generate an API key to make an API Request.

title: Copper API review: contact caps and 180 a minute
snippet:
Requests are limited to 180 a minute on a rolling window, the same on every plan that has the API. What the plan changes is how many contacts you may store: 2,500 on Basic, 15,000 on Professional, unlimited on Business.

Authentication is an API key sent in three custom headers, or OAuth 2.0 for applications other people install. Copper calls the product the Developer API, and its documentation lives at developer.copper.com, with a Postman collection to start from.

A Copper user's access can be restricted by team permissions, and the API honors those restrictions. Copper's own advice is to use an admin's credentials for integrations, and to create a separate, non-personal user so records written through the API are owned by the integration rather than by a person.
## Copper API pricing, plan by plan
Copper API pricing is seat pricing: the API comes with the subscription, and the plan you choose sets the contact cap rather than the request rate.
### Basic
$23
/seat/mo billed annually, $29 month to month
- 2,500 contact limit
- Pipelines and task automation
- Contact enrichment
### Professional
$59
/seat/mo billed annually, $69 month to month
- 15,000 contact limit
- Workflow automation, bulk email and reporting
- Integrations
### Business
$99
/seat/mo billed annually, $134 month to month
- Unlimited contacts
- Email series and custom reports
- Multi-currency and premium support
Annual billing takes up to 26% off, and every plan starts with a free trial; there is no free tier after it. Copper says 63% of customers start on Professional, which is also the first plan whose card lists integrations. Its feature comparison names the API and embedded integration SDK as a feature, but the capture read for this review does not show which plans carry it, so confirm the plan before building.

Is the Copper API free?
No free tier. Free trial, and annual billing takes up to 26% off. Paid plans start at $23/seat/mo annual.
How much does the Copper API cost?
Copper starts at $23/seat/mo annual. It bills per seat, by subscription. Read from Copper's own pricing page on 24 October 2026.

title: Create an API key
snippet:
To access the Copper API, you need to have an API key. To create an API key, go to the [Copper Platform UI](https://platform.copper.co/) and follow these steps:
1
Go to organisation settings
On your Copper dashboard, click your organisation’s name in the top left of your screen, select **Organisation settings**, and then select **API Keys**.

2
Choose the owner, set permissions, and configure an IP allowlist
Determine if the API key should be associated with your personal account or a service user account. Optionally, you can restrict its access to specific IP addresses by setting IP addresses restrictions.

title: bit-integrations.com/blog/gravity-forms-copper-crm-integration
snippet:
You can **connect Gravity Forms to Copper CRM** in three ways. All three need a Copper plan with API access (trial, Professional, or Business; Basic will not work). Pick what you need:

**All three methods depend on Copper features that are gated by plan.** Copper documents Developer API access on its trial, Professional, and Business plans.
The free trial grants temporary access to Professional and Business-level features, including the API, which is how this article’s Bit Integrations test ran on a Business-plan trial.
Copper Basic and Starter do not include API access. Copper separately lists the Outfunnel connector as available on Professional and Business only.
**Buying Outfunnel, Gravity Extra, or Bit Integrations does not add the integration to a Copper Basic account.** Because this rule governs every method below, it is stated here once instead of being repeated in each section.
